concepts.name: Tenant Registry (Träger)
concepts.summary: A tenant is one Träger (carrier organisation) running its own counselling offering on the shared platform. TenantEntity plus TenantRepository hold the canonical record, while TenantService and TenantServiceFacade wrap all reads and writes; TenantConverter maps between the JPA entity and the generated OpenAPI DTOs. Subdomain, licensing and content fields on the entity are what every other ORISO service resolves a tenant by.

concepts.name: Tenant Context Resolution
concepts.summary: Every request must be attributed to exactly one tenant before authorisation can run. TenantResolverService chains the concrete TenantResolver implementations — AccessTokenTenantResolver (tenantId claim in the Keycloak JWT), SubdomainTenantResolver (via SubdomainExtractor) and CookieTenantResolver — and the first resolver that yields an id wins. TenantHeaderSupplier propagates the resolved id on outgoing calls to downstream ORISO services.

concepts.name: Keycloak JWT Authorisation
concepts.summary: The service is an OAuth2 resource server against Keycloak: WebSecurityConfig wires the filter chain and JwtAuthConverter turns realm roles into Spring authorities using RoleAuthorizationAuthorityMapper, Authority and UserRole. Endpoint-level checks live in AuthorisationService, and tenant-scoped rules (may this tenant admin touch this tenant id?) in TenantFacadeAuthorisationService.

concepts.name: Tenant Settings and Admin Controls
concepts.summary: TenantSettings and TenantSetting describe the per-tenant feature switches persisted as JSON on the tenant row, while TenantAdminControlsEntity plus TenantAdminControlsSettings and TenantAdminAllowedPermissionTogglesSettings define which of those switches a tenant admin is allowed to change at all. TenantAdminControlsService serves GET/PUT /tenantadmin/controls, and TenantFacadeDependentSettingsOverrideService forces dependent settings off when their prerequisite is disabled.

concepts.name: Theming and Branding Inheritance
concepts.summary: Tenants carry colours, logos and login effects that may be inherited from a parent or platform default. EffectiveThemingApplier computes the effective theme, InheritedBrandingEchoStripper removes values a tenant merely echoed from its parent so they are not stored as local overrides, and BrandingAssetDecoder plus PublicBrandingAssetService serve the decoded assets on GET /tenant/public/branding/{asset}. Liquibase changesets addThemingAccentAndSignal.sql and addThemingLoginEffect.sql added the newer theme columns.

concepts.name: Tenant Permission Policies
concepts.summary: Beyond plain booleans, permissions are modelled as policies: PermissionFeature names the feature, PermissionPolicyMode says whether it is forced, defaulted or free, and PermissionPolicyResolver combines them into a ResolvedPolicyValue. TenantPermissionPolicyService persists them through TenantPermissionPolicyRepository into the tenant_permission_policy table, LegacyPermissionPolicyMapper bridges the older boolean settings, and EffectivePermissionSettingsApplier stamps the outcome onto outgoing DTOs.

concepts.name: Data Processing Agreement (DPA/AVV) Lifecycle
concepts.summary: A tenant's DPA is versioned and signed. TenantDpaVersionEntity holds the published versions, TenantDpaSignatureEntity and TenantDpaAdminSignatureEntity the signatures, and TenantDpaStatus plus DpaSignatureStatus the state machine. TenantDpaService and TenantDpaStatusService own the rules, GoverningDpaResolver decides which version currently binds a tenant, and TenantDpaFacade exposes the whole thing under /tenantadmin/{id}/dpa/*.

concepts.name: Token-Based External DPA Confirmation
concepts.summary: A DPA can be forwarded to someone who has no admin account: DpaSignToken mints and validates the opaque token stored with the signature row, DpaSignatureOwnership decides who the signature belongs to, and InvalidDpaSignTokenException plus DpaNotPublishedException reject stale or premature links. The public endpoints GET/POST /tenant/public/dpa/confirm/{token} and POST /tenant/public/dpa/forward are the unauthenticated surface for it.

concepts.name: Platform DPIA Master Data
concepts.summary: The DSFA/DPIA master data that is identical for the whole platform lives in PlatformDpiaMasterDataEntity, backed by the platform_dpia_master_data table created in createPlatformDpiaMasterData.sql. PlatformDpiaMasterDataService and PlatformDpiaMasterDataFacade serve GET/PUT /tenantadmin/dpia and the read-only GET /tenant/public/dpia, with PlatformDpiaMasterDataConverter and DpiaMasterDataJacksonConfig handling the nested JSON structure.

concepts.name: Tenant ID Allocation and Reservation
concepts.summary: Tenant ids are not simply auto-increment: TenantIdAllocationService hands out the next free id and can reserve one ahead of tenant creation, storing TenantIdReservationEntity rows (TenantIdReservationStatus, TenantIdAllocationStatus) via TenantIdReservationRepository. AssignedOrSequenceIdGenerator lets an explicitly assigned id win over the sequence, and TenantIdAllocationConflictException / TenantIdAllocationExhaustedException surface the failure cases.

concepts.name: Tenant Media Assets
concepts.summary: Logos and similar uploads are stored in the database as TenantMediaEntity rows (table created by createTenantMediaTable.sql) rather than on a file share. TenantMediaService validates the payload — rejecting with MediaSizeLimitExceededException or UnsupportedMediaContentException — and TenantMediaController serves the binary back on GET /media/{mediaId} while POST /tenantadmin/media accepts new uploads.

concepts.name: AI-Assisted Content Translation
concepts.summary: Multilingual tenant content can be machine-translated through a pluggable TranslationProviderClient, implemented by OpenAiCompatibleChatClient with MistralClient and OpenRouterClient as concrete providers. TranslationService and TranslationFacade drive POST /tenantadmin/translate and the provider key management under /tenantadmin/translation/keys, TranslationMetaUtil records translation metadata, and ApiKeyMasker keeps keys out of responses and logs.

flows.name: Tenant admin edits a tenant → validated, sanitised record persisted
flows.summary: POST/PUT /tenantadmin and GET /tenantadmin/{id} enter TenantController, which delegates to TenantServiceFacade. The facade runs TenantFacadeAuthorisationService for the tenant-scope check, TenantInputSanitizer (on top of InputSanitizer) for HTML sanitising, TenantFacadeChangeDetectionService to see what actually changed, then TenantService and TenantRepository for persistence, with TenantConverter mapping DTO to TenantEntity.

flows.name: Anonymous frontend loads tenant branding → restricted public payload
flows.summary: GET /tenant/public/{subdomain}, /tenant/public/single and /tenant/public/id/{tenantId} are served by TenantController without authentication. TenantServiceFacade builds a TenantRestrictedData / TenantRestrictedDataView projection, SingleDomainTenantOverrideService substitutes the configured single-domain tenant when the platform runs non-multitenant, and RestrictedPublicTenantJacksonConfig strips everything not meant for anonymous callers.

flows.name: Tenant admin signs the DPA → gate opens for the tenant
flows.summary: POST /tenantadmin/{id}/dpa/invite and POST /tenantadmin/{id}/dpa/sign reach TenantDpaFacade through TenantController. The facade asks GoverningDpaResolver which TenantDpaVersionEntity binds, writes a TenantDpaAdminSignatureEntity through TenantDpaAdminSignatureRepository, and TenantDpaStatusService recomputes the status that GET /tenantadmin/{id}/dpa/gate reports back to the Admin Panel.

flows.name: External signer confirms a forwarded DPA → signature recorded without login
flows.summary: POST /tenant/public/dpa/forward creates a signature row carrying a token minted by DpaSignToken; the recipient opens GET /tenant/public/dpa/confirm/{token} and posts back to the same path. TenantDpaFacade validates the token and DpaSignatureOwnership, persists via TenantDpaSignatureRepository, and DpaSignedNoticeHintService supplies the confirmation notice text; TenantDpaRetentionService later prunes expired rows.

flows.name: Operator reserves a tenant id → id held until the tenant is created
flows.summary: GET /tenantadmin/tenant-ids/{id}/availability and POST /tenantadmin/tenant-ids/reservations go from TenantController into TenantIdAllocationService, which writes a TenantIdReservationEntity through TenantIdReservationRepository. Conflicting or exhausted ranges raise TenantIdAllocationConflictException or TenantIdAllocationExhaustedException, which ExceptionHandlerAdvice maps to HTTP status codes; DELETE .../reservations/{id} releases the hold.

flows.name: Tenant admin changes a permission → allowlist checked, policy resolved
flows.summary: PUT /tenantadmin/{id}/permission-policies enters TenantController and TenantPermissionPolicyService. The allowlist in TenantAdminAllowedPermissionTogglesSettings, served by TenantAdminControlsService, decides whether the toggle may be changed at all; PermissionPolicyResolver then folds the stored TenantPermissionPolicyEntity rows and the legacy booleans into the effective value returned on GET.

flows.name: Tenant admin uploads a logo → stored row served back by media id
flows.summary: POST /tenantadmin/media arrives at TenantController, TenantMediaService checks size and content type and persists a TenantMediaEntity through TenantMediaRepository. The stored id is then referenced from the tenant's branding fields, and TenantMediaController streams the bytes on GET /media/{mediaId} for anonymous frontend callers.

flows.name: Tenant admin translates content → provider key decrypted, text returned
flows.summary: POST /tenantadmin/translate reaches TranslationFacade, which loads the configured provider key, decrypts it with TranslationApiKeyEncryptionService and calls the matching TranslationProviderClient (OpenAiCompatibleChatClient against Mistral or OpenRouter). Failures become a TranslationException carrying a TranslationErrorCode; ApiKeyMasker ensures the key never reaches the response of GET /tenantadmin/translation/keys.

flows.name: Per-tenant SMTP credentials stored → encrypted at rest, read back masked
flows.summary: TenantSmtpSettings hangs off the tenant settings JSON; SmtpPasswordEncryptionService encrypts the password before it is written and decrypts it on read, while SmtpPasswordEncryptionMigration re-encrypts rows that predate the scheme at startup. The consumed Application Settings contract (GET /settingsadmin/smtp-credentials, PATCH /settingsadmin) is the shared-settings counterpart, and ApplicationSettingsService pushes changes on to that downstream API.

flows.name: Tenant change propagates → consulting types and admin users updated
flows.summary: When TenantServiceFacade detects a relevant change it calls out through the API clients built by ConsultingTypeServiceApiControllerFactory, UserAdminServiceApiControllerFactory and ApplicationSettingsApiControllerFactory. ConsultingTypeService and UserAdminService add the tenant header via TenantHeaderSupplier and the auth header via SecurityHeaderSupplier; failures surface as ConsultingTypeCommunicationException or ApplicationSettingsUpdateException.

layerDescriptions.Domain Concepts: Coarse, hand-curated concepts and flows that describe what the TenantService means for Träger administration rather than which files it contains.
layerDescriptions.API Endpoints: The 108 REST operations declared in the OpenAPI specifications, spanning the service's own /tenant, /tenantadmin, /media and /settings routes plus the consumed contracts of the agency, user-admin and consulting-type services.
layerDescriptions.API Layer: All request-facing Java code under com.vi.tenantservice.api: controllers, facades, services, converters, JPA entities and repositories, tenant resolution, policies and input sanitising.
layerDescriptions.Core: The Spring Boot entry point TenantServiceApplication plus repository-level build, deployment and CI scripts such as check-version.sh, deploy-development.sh and the scripts/ci helpers.
layerDescriptions.Configuration Layer: The com.vi.tenantservice.config package: ConfigurationValidator and the Keycloak-backed security wiring (WebSecurityConfig, JwtAuthConverter, AuthorisationService, KeycloakLogoutHandler).
layerDescriptions.Test Layer: Java and Python test code, including the Liquibase changeset immutability guard, deployment schema checks and the CI contract/coverage guards.
